Vidya

subtype: Approach: active recall with mock tests [Action]

subtype: Approach: active recall with mock tests [Action]

Tutor's note, 22 February — Karthik, Class 12 Physics
Since 1 February Karthik has written a full timed paper every alternate day in my back room, and marked it himself with the official scheme while I watched. Eleven papers so far. He records the marks lost per topic in a table. The early papers told a clear story: optics numericals leaking marks every time, while mechanics stayed strong. He admitted he had been "resting" on mechanics before, because it felt safe. For the last ten days he has spent his non-paper days almost entirely on optics, and his optics section has gone from about half marks to nearly full. His overall score has risen from 41 to 56 out of 70. I have suggested one easy day before the exam, with no full paper.
— Bhupen

qa.q: How many papers has Karthik written so far?
qa.a: Eleven papers.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel about mechanics before the mock papers?
qa.a: He felt safe and comfortable with mechanics, which is why he kept resting on it.

qa.q: Why does targeting optics work better than general revision?
qa.a: The table shows optics is where marks leak, so focused practice there raises the score far more than rereading strong topics.

qa.q: How does Bhupen see Karthik's progress?
qa.a: Bhupen tracks the rise from 41 to 56 and suggests an easy day before the exam, caring about rest as well as scores.

grounding: A tutor's note shows timed mock papers every alternate day revealing which topic slips, so revision becomes targeted.

subtype: Approach: pre-mortem before the plan starts [Thinking]

"Imagine it's exam morning," she said, "and revision went badly. Why?" Ivan closed his eyes. "I was on my phone every night till one." He wrote it down. "I got sick in week two and lost five days." Down. "I stayed up cramming and was a zombie." Down. Then Mina said, "Now fix each one before it happens." Phone: charges in the hallway after ten. Sick week: every Sunday afternoon left free for catch-up. Sleep: lights out at eleven, written on the fridge. Ivan looked at the sheet. It felt odd to plan for failure, but now the plan had shields.

subtype: Approach: contingency planning for illness or power cuts [Thinking]

"Ma'am, can I show you something?" Rajni held out her planner. "It's the fifteenth. I was supposed to have finished twelve chapters. I've done eight."
Avni Ma'am looked at it. "Four behind. What's left?"
"Coordination compounds, polymers, everyday chemistry, surface chemistry, and the big ones, electrochemistry and kinetics."
"Have you looked at the last ten papers?"
"Yes. Electrochemistry and kinetics come every year. Polymers and everyday chemistry are a few marks, and hardly ever asked."
"So what do you want to do?"
Rajni took a breath. "Drop polymers and everyday chemistry for now. Put those hours into electrochemistry and kinetics. Is that okay?"
"It's a sensible trade. Read their summaries once at the end if you have time."
Rajni crossed two lines off the planner. "I feel less behind already."

To make Uday feel bad? For a minute, yes. Then, underneath: for Uday to understand. To be able to trust him again. Counsellor's note, 9 August — Gautam, Class 10
Gautam came to see me on Monday. His best friend Neeraj had told the football team that Gautam was afraid of deep water, something Gautam had shared in confidence. He wanted to "have it out" in front of everyone. We talked about what he actually wanted, and he said, "For him to get why it mattered." So we practised. Today I saw them on the bench by the office after school, just the two of them. From the door I heard Gautam say, "I felt stupid when the team found out. I'd only told you." Then, "What happened?" Neeraj's shoulders, which had been up by his ears, came down. They talked for about twenty minutes. Afterwards both came in to borrow the football, together. I will check in with Gautam on Friday.
— Vijay
